audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 10, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for anointing and kiss, sign sequence, prophetic-band altered state, identity-change language, Gilgal waiting instruction, private secrecy, public lot, hiding among baggage, height rhetoric, acclamation, royal custom, dissent, and mental-health/leader-cult safeguards.

verses.restored: Samuel took flask of oil, poured it upon Saul's head, kissed him, and said, Has not YHWH anointed you as leader over his inheritance?

familiar.text: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the LORD hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?

modern.text: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת פַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶן וַיִּצֹ֥ק עַל רֹאשׁ֖וֹ וַיִּשָּׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲל֗וֹא כִּֽי מְשָׁחֲךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה עַל נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְנָגִֽיד

verses.restored: When you go from me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb in border of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will say to you, Donkeys you went to seek are found, and look, your father has left matter of donkeys and is anxious for you, saying, What shall I do about my son?

familiar.text: When thou art departed from me to day, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel’s sepulchre in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say unto thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found: and, lo, thy father hath left the care of the asses, and sorroweth for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?

modern.text: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?”’

original.text: בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֤ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵעִמָּדִ֔י וּמָצָאתָ֩ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲנָשִׁ֜ים עִם קְבֻרַ֥ת רָחֵ֛ל בִּגְב֥וּל בִּנְיָמִ֖ן בְּצֶלְצַ֑ח וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ נִמְצְא֤וּ הָאֲתֹנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֣כְתָּ לְבַקֵּ֔שׁ וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָטַ֤שׁ אָבִ֨יךָ֙ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֣י הָאֲתֹנ֔וֹת וְדָאַ֤ג לָכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לִבְנִֽי

verses.restored: You shall pass on from there and come to oak of Tabor. Three men going up to Divine at Bethel will meet you, one carrying three young goats, one carrying three loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.

familiar.text: Then shalt thou go on forward from thence, and thou shalt come to the plain of Tabor, and there shall meet thee three men going up to God to Bethel, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:

modern.text: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.

original.text: וְחָלַפְתָּ֨ מִשָּׁ֜ם וָהָ֗לְאָה וּבָ֨אתָ֙ עַד אֵל֣וֹן תָּב֔וֹר וּמְצָא֤וּךָ שָּׁם֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים אֶל הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל אֶחָ֞ד נֹשֵׂ֣א שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְדָיִ֗ים וְאֶחָד֙ נֹשֵׂ֗א שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙ כִּכְּר֣וֹת לֶ֔חֶם וְאֶחָ֥ד נֹשֵׂ֖א נֵֽבֶל יָֽיִן

verses.restored: They will ask about your well-being and give you two loaves of bread, and you shall take them from their hand.

familiar.text: And they will salute thee, and give thee two loaves of bread; which thou shalt receive of their hands.

modern.text: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.

original.text: וְשָׁאֲל֥וּ לְךָ֖ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וְנָתְנ֤וּ לְךָ֙ שְׁתֵּי לֶ֔חֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מִיָּדָֽם

verses.restored: Afterward you shall come to hill of Divine where Philistine garrison is. As you come there to city, you will meet a band of prophets coming down from high place, with harp, tambourine, flute, and lyre before them, and they will be prophesying.

familiar.text: After that thou shalt come to the hill of God, where is the garrison of the Philistines: and it shall come to pass, when thou art come thither to the city, that thou shalt meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a tabret, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they shall prophesy:

modern.text: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.

original.text: אַ֣חַר כֵּ֗ן תָּבוֹא֙ גִּבְעַ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֖ם נְצִבֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וִיהִי֩ כְבֹאֲךָ֨ שָׁ֜ם הָעִ֗יר וּפָגַעְתָּ֞ חֶ֤בֶל נְבִיאִים֙ יֹרְדִ֣ים מֵֽהַבָּמָ֔ה וְלִפְנֵיהֶ֞ם נֵ֤בֶל וְתֹף֙ וְחָלִ֣יל וְכִנּ֔וֹר וְהֵ֖מָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִֽים

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

modern.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.

original.text: וְצָלְחָ֤ה עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וְהִתְנַבִּ֖יתָ עִמָּ֑ם וְנֶהְפַּכְתָּ֖ לְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵֽר

verses.restored: When these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds, for Divine is with you.

familiar.text: And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee.

modern.text: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּ֥י תבאינה הָאֹת֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָ֑ךְ עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּמְצָ֣א יָדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: You shall go down before me to Gilgal, and look, I will come down to you to offer ascending offerings and sacrifice peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you and make known to you what you shall do.

familiar.text: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do.

modern.text: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.” Samuel’s Signs Fulfilled

original.text: וְיָרַדְתָּ֣ לְפָנַי֮ הַגִּלְגָּל֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ יֹרֵ֣ד אֵלֶ֔יךָ לְהַעֲל֣וֹת עֹל֔וֹת לִזְבֹּ֖חַ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֑ים שִׁבְעַ֨ת יָמִ֤ים תּוֹחֵל֙ עַד בּוֹאִ֣י אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהוֹדַעְתִּ֣י לְךָ֔ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: It happened as he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, Divine turned for him another heart, and all these signs came that day.

familiar.text: And it was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.

modern.text: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּהַפְנֹת֤וֹ שִׁכְמוֹ֙ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ מֵעִ֣ם שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיַּהֲפָךְ ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵ֣ב אַחֵ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ כָּל הָאֹת֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: They came there to hill, and look, a band of prophets met him. Spirit of Divine rushed upon him, and he prophesied among them.

familiar.text: And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a company of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them.

modern.text: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ שָׁם֙ הַגִּבְעָ֔תָה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֶֽבֶל נְבִאִ֖ים לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַתִּצְלַ֤ח עָלָיו֙ ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֖א בְּתוֹכָֽם

verses.restored: It happened, when all who knew him before saw, and look, he prophesied with prophets, people said each to companion, What is this that has happened to son of Kish? Is Saul also among prophets?

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?

modern.text: All those who had formerly known Saul and saw him prophesying with the prophets asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כָּל יֽוֹדְעוֹ֙ מֵאִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֔וֹם וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה עִם נְבִאִ֖ים נִבָּ֑א וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֗הוּ מַה זֶּה֙ הָיָ֣ה לְבֶן קִ֔ישׁ הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִיאִֽים

verses.restored: A man from there answered and said, And who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among prophets?

familiar.text: And one of the same place answered and said, But who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

modern.text: Then a man who lived there replied, “And who is their father?” So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן אִ֥ישׁ מִשָּׁ֛ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר וּמִ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם עַל כֵּן֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֔ל הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִאִֽים

verses.restored: When he finished prophesying, he came to high place.

familiar.text: And when he had made an end of prophesying, he came to the high place.

modern.text: And when Saul had finished prophesying, he went up to the high place.

original.text: וַיְכַל֙ מֵֽהִתְנַבּ֔וֹת וַיָּבֹ֖א הַבָּמָֽה

verses.restored: Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, Where did you go? He said, To seek donkeys; when we saw they were not found, we went to Samuel.

familiar.text: And Saul’s uncle said unto him and to his servant, Whither went ye? And he said, To seek the asses: and when we saw that they were no where, we came to Samuel.

modern.text: Now Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” “To look for the donkeys,” Saul replied. “When we saw they were not to be found, we went to Samuel.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דּ֨וֹד שָׁא֥וּל אֵלָ֛יו וְאֶֽל נַעֲר֖וֹ אָ֣ן הֲלַכְתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲתֹנ֔וֹת וַנִּרְאֶ֣ה כִי אַ֔יִן וַנָּב֖וֹא אֶל שְׁמוּאֵֽל

verses.restored: Saul's uncle said, Tell me, please, what Samuel said to you.

familiar.text: And Saul’s uncle said, Tell me, I pray thee, what Samuel said unto you.

modern.text: “Tell me,” Saul’s uncle asked, “what did Samuel say to you?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דּ֣וֹד שָׁא֑וּל הַגִּֽידָה נָּ֣א לִ֔י מָֽה אָמַ֥ר לָכֶ֖ם שְׁמוּאֵֽל

verses.restored: Saul said to his uncle, He plainly told us donkeys had been found. But matter of kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

modern.text: And Saul replied, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship. Saul Proclaimed King

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל דּוֹד֔וֹ הַגֵּ֤ד הִגִּיד֙ לָ֔נוּ כִּ֥י נִמְצְא֖וּ הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאֶת דְּבַ֤ר הַמְּלוּכָה֙ לֹֽא הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר שְׁמוּאֵֽל

verses.restored: Samuel called people together to YHWH at Mizpah.

familiar.text: And Samuel called the people together unto the LORD to Mizpeh;

modern.text: After this, Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah

original.text: וַיַּצְעֵ֤ק שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם אֶל יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּֽה

verses.restored: He said to children of Israel, Thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I rescued you from hand of Egypt and from hand of all kingdoms oppressing you.

familiar.text: And said unto the children of Israel, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you:

modern.text: and said to the Israelites, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I rescued you from the hands of the Egyptians and of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָנֹכִ֛י הֶעֱלֵ֥יתִי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וָאַצִּ֤יל אֶתְכֶם֙ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִיַּד֙ כָּל הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת הַלֹּחֲצִ֖ים אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: But today you have rejected your Divine, who saves you from all your evils and distresses, and you have said, No, but set a king over us. Now present yourselves before YHWH by tribes and thousands/clans.

familiar.text: And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes, and by your thousands.

modern.text: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans.”

original.text: וְאַתֶּ֨ם הַיּ֜וֹם מְאַסְתֶּ֣ם אֶת אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר ה֣וּא מוֹשִׁ֣יעַ לָכֶם֮ מִכָּל רָעוֹתֵיכֶ֣ם וְצָרֹֽתֵיכֶם֒ וַתֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ כִּי מֶ֖לֶךְ תָּשִׂ֣ים עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה הִֽתְיַצְּבוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֖ם וּלְאַלְפֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Samuel brought near all tribes of Israel, and tribe of Benjamin was taken.

familiar.text: And when Samuel had caused all the tribes of Israel to come near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

modern.text: Thus Samuel had all the tribes of Israel come forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected.

original.text: וַיַּקְרֵ֣ב שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד שֵׁ֥בֶט בִּנְיָמִֽן

verses.restored: He brought near tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and clan of Matrites was taken; then Saul son of Kish was taken. They sought him, but he was not found.

familiar.text: When he had caused the tribe of Benjamin to come near by their families, the family of Matri was taken, and Saul the son of Kish was taken: and when they sought him, he could not be found.

modern.text: Then he had the tribe of Benjamin come forward by its clans, and the clan of Matri was selected. Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected. But when they looked for him, they could not find him.

original.text: וַיַּקְרֵ֞ב אֶת שֵׁ֤בֶט בִּנְיָמִן֙ למשפחתו וַתִּלָּכֵ֖ד מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַמַּטְרִ֑י וַיִּלָּכֵד֙ שָׁא֣וּל בֶּן קִ֔ישׁ וַיְבַקְשֻׁ֖הוּ וְלֹ֥א נִמְצָֽא

verses.restored: They inquired again of YHWH, Has another man come here? YHWH said, Look, he has hidden himself among baggage.

familiar.text: Therefore they enquired of the LORD further, if the man should yet come thither. And the LORD answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff.

modern.text: So again they inquired of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?” And the LORD replied, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ עוֹד֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה הֲבָ֥א ע֖וֹד הֲלֹ֣ם אִ֑ישׁ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּה ה֥וּא נֶחְבָּ֖א אֶל הַכֵּלִֽים

verses.restored: They ran and took him from there. He stood among people, and he was taller than all people from his shoulders upward.

familiar.text: And they ran and fetched him thence: and when he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.

modern.text: So they ran and brought Saul, and when he stood among the people, he was a head taller than any of the others.

original.text: וַיָּרֻ֨צוּ֙ וַיִּקָּחֻ֣הוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֖ב בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּגְבַּהּ֙ מִכָּל הָעָ֔ם מִשִּׁכְמ֖וֹ וָמָֽעְלָה

verses.restored: Samuel said to all people, Have you seen whom YHWH has chosen? There is none like him among all people. All people shouted and said, Let king live!

familiar.text: And Samuel said to all the people, See ye him whom the LORD hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people? And all the people shouted, and said, God save the king.

modern.text: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶל כָּל הָעָ֗ם הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽחַר בּ֣וֹ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין כָּמֹ֖הוּ בְּכָל הָעָ֑ם וַיָּרִ֧עוּ כָל הָעָ֛ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Samuel spoke to people judgment/custom of kingship, wrote it in book, and placed it before YHWH. Samuel sent all people away, each to house.

familiar.text: Then Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

modern.text: Then Samuel explained to the people the rights of kingship. He wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶל הָעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמְּלֻכָ֔ה וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וַיַּנַּ֖ח לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּ֧ח שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶת כָּל הָעָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and the force/valiant ones whose hearts Divine had touched went with him.

familiar.text: And Saul also went home to Gibeah; and there went with him a band of men, whose hearts God had touched.

modern.text: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, and the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.

original.text: וְגַ֨ם שָׁא֔וּל הָלַ֥ךְ לְבֵית֖וֹ גִּבְעָ֑תָה וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ הַחַ֕יִל אֲשֶׁר נָגַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבָּֽם

verses.restored: But worthless men said, How will this one save us? They despised him and brought him no gift. But he was as one silent.

familiar.text: But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he held his peace.

modern.text: But some worthless men said, “How can this man save us?” So they despised him and brought him no gifts; but Saul remained silent about it.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֧י בְלִיַּ֣עַל אָמְר֗וּ מַה יֹּשִׁעֵ֨נוּ֙ זֶ֔ה וַיִּבְזֻ֕הוּ וְלֹֽא הֵבִ֥יאוּ ל֖וֹ מִנְחָ֑ה וַיְהִ֖י כְּמַחֲרִֽישׁ

translation_notes: The private anointing, public lot, prophetic experience, and popular acclamation are distinct legitimating scenes; none removes the need for accountability.
Samuel's kiss is an ancient greeting/commission gesture, not permission for leaders to cross bodily boundaries.
Prophetic music and altered behavior are communal religious phenomena, not diagnostic evidence of mental illness or automatic proof of holiness.
'Turned into another man' and 'another heart' describe vocational transformation; they must not erase identity, consent, or responsibility.
The instruction to do what the hand finds is limited by the surrounding commission and cannot authorize impulsive or violent behavior.
Saul hides among baggage. Fear, reluctance, overwhelm, or privacy do not disqualify a person or prove false humility.
Public selection by lot reflects ancient discernment and cannot replace transparent, participatory governance.
Saul's height again attracts attention; bodily traits are not leadership qualifications.
'Let the king live' is political acclamation, not worship.
The 'judgment/custom of kingship' should be read beside chapter 8's warning about royal extraction.
The dissenters' insult does not justify suppression, retaliation, or compulsory gifts; Saul's silence initially restrains escalation.
safety_note: Do not use anointing, prophecy, altered states, lots, bodily appearance, crowd acclaim, or claims that Divine touched supporters' hearts to demand political obedience. Do not stigmatize Saul's hiding or prophetic behavior as mental illness. Dissent is not treason, and leaders may not punish people for withholding praise or gifts.
